title: Introduce guided tool-debugger, authored scenario templates, and inline eval playground
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Adds a lightweight browser-based tool debugger and a set of authored scenario templates for guided authoring. Includes a small inline eval runner and telemetry probes to help teams validate tool-calling behavior before promoting to production.
description:
Motivation: engineers and authors frequently need a small, deterministic playground to debug agent tool-calling flows and to iterate on authored scenario templates with built-in telemetry. This PR adds a compact guided tool debugger (browser UI + stubbed tool adapters), a curated set of authored scenario templates for common RAG/agent patterns, and an inline eval runner so prompt/tool changes can be validated locally with small synthetic corpora.

What I changed: added a minimal browser-based debugger that can run an agent against stubbed tools (http webhook, SQL runner, file lookup) with deterministic seeds and stepwise traces. Included eight authored scenario templates (FAQ-bot, multimodal-note-collector, incremental-index-search, policy-enforced-toolchain, embedded-calculator, email-drafter-with-actions, paginated-retriever, and a streaming-resume-handler) plus a compact inline eval harness that executes scenario steps and emits structured assertions. All templates include sample telemetry probes and suggested tracing points for the Redwood Console integration.

Why this is useful: teams can now iterate on tool specs and prompt scaffolding without firing up full backend services or a Dedicated deployment. The debugger surfaces the sequence of tool calls, argument payloads, and the model's structured outputs so authors can quickly identify mismatch between tool contracts and agent behavior. The inline eval runner makes it easy to add small acceptance tests to CI or run locally before opening a larger PR.

Compatibility and migration notes: this change is additive and opt-in. Templates live under examples/guided-tool-debugger/templates and will not affect existing quickstarts. The debugger uses existing SDK shims and a light-weight wasm shim for sandboxed adapters. If a team wants to persist telemetry from the playground to Redwood Console, they must enable the sandbox telemetry flag in their dev account (docs link included below).

Checklist:
- [x] Add playground UI and wasm shim for stubbed adapters
- [x] Ship eight authored scenario templates with metadata and seed corpora
- [x] Add inline eval runner and a compact assertion DSL
- [x] Include telemetry probe examples and README with integration steps
- [x] Add unit tests for inline runner and CI smoke job
- [x] Update docs site quickstart page to reference the new playground

Files and docs referenced: README: docs/guided-tool-debugger/README.md (authoring steps, telemetry), Templates: examples/guided-tool-debugger/templates/*.yaml, Playground UI: examples/guided-tool-debugger/ui/*, Inline eval: examples/guided-tool-debugger/eval/runner.py, CI job: .github/workflows/playground-smoke.yml. Playground docs will be linked from devloop: https://docs.redwood.ai/devloop/guided-tool-debugger

Security notes: the sandboxed adapter only runs locally and the UI runs in the browser; by default no external network calls are allowed except to configured webhook stubs. The wasm adapter enforces a strict capability manifest. Teams that opt to enable remote telemetry must follow the private data checklist in docs/guided-tool-debugger/security.md.

Manual testing notes: see examples/guided-tool-debugger/TESTING.md for step-by-step smoke steps. The inline eval runner includes a seeded corpus so test runs are deterministic by default.
